_doc: C272 — progression ladders, data only. The engine does NOT select from this file yet: the exercises it introduces carry role 'ladder' (bodyweight levels) or 'library' (technique / try-hard / pocket drills), which no template block requests. Claude Code reads it through backend/engine/athlete_context.py (current level per family, seeded read-only from history and tests) and the /custom-session command. level_idx starts at 0. A later A brief turns the bodyweight ladders into a closed loop (bw_progression state, R0-R12 of the BW spec).

seed_rules.tested_gate: an official max (retest_policy.official_max, test log < 90 days) on the finger or pulling protocol
seed_rules.history_dose_rule: last completed dose minus one step, never the bottom of the band
seed_rules.test_target_rule: about test / 3 on the entry level (ENGINEERING CONSTANT)

history_aliases.why: hanging_leg_raise is the straight-legs-to-bar movement (catalog note 'straight legs to bar'; C273 aligned its cues to the note); the to-horizontal level is hanging_leg_raise_horizontal. No cut-off date: the alias holds for every log.

lever_hold.source: ENGINEERING CONSTANT step; 15 s criterion aligned with the front_lever_tuck catalog note (4x15 s)

max_core.source: dragon flag / front lever dynamic tutorials

nordic.source: Presland 2018: low-volume Nordic training gives the same adaptation

gates.why: pike mobility is the real limit
pike mobility is the real limit

families.label: Hanging compression (knee raise → toes to bar)

levels.note: ring height is part of the dose: hip, thigh, knee (lower = harder) — ENGINEERING CONSTANT

families.label: Dragon flag (needs a bench)
families.notes: v_up leaves this ladder and stays a fixed compression exercise.

families.label: Hollow / plank (warm-up only for advanced athletes)
sources: Schoenfeld B, Contreras B (2014), Strength Cond J — RKC plank EMG
families.notes: Below the core intensity floor for athletes with l_sit ≥ 35 s: warm-up and deload only when alternatives exist.

families.label: Front lever

terminal.why: ankle weights load the elbow distally

families.notes: Every level (and raise / row / negative) counts as a heavy pull: athlete_context adds it to the heavy-pull days of a tested athlete, so it counts in the 2 heavy pulls per 7 days of the context guards. NOT counted by retest_policy (the pull-up retest blocker is load-based, engine-wide): keep it 48 h away from a pull-up test by hand. Never in the 24 h before limit / strength_long and at most 1 per week in performance are manual rules (ENGINEERING CONSTANT). Seed only from history (the pulling ratio is too weak a proxy for an elbow-risk skill).

families.label: Lateral (side plank → Copenhagen)
sources: Harøy J et al. (2019), Br J Sports Med
families.notes: Entering at the Copenhagen: 2 sessions of the short lever at 3x15 s first (groin risk, Harøy 2019).

families.label: Posterior chain (antagonist of compression)
families.notes: A core block with 2 compression exercises must include one exercise of this family.

families.label: Anti-rotation (Pallof)
families.notes: Needs a band (band / resistance_band) or a cable.

families.label: Rotation (windshield wipers)
families.notes: Level 2 is terminal and optional (catalog safety note: flexion + rotation).

families.label: Horizontal push (antagonist)
families.notes: Antagonist at RIR 2-3: easy raises the reps, no promotion above intensity 'high'. One-arm push-up and pseudo-planche stay builder-only.

gates.requires_note: wall handstand hold of at least 30 s

families.label: Dip
families.notes: Dip equipment keys (dip bars / parallel bars) are a later A brief.

families.label: Bodyweight pull (only athletes WITHOUT a tested 2RM)
families.notes: A tested athlete keeps weighted_pullup with the anchored load (B364). Lock-offs at open angles only. From L3 (one-arm) a heavy pull for the context guards of a tested athlete (same rule as front_lever).

families.label: Single-leg squat
families.notes: pistol_squat_progression stays active (body-part picker) until the A brief updates it.

families.label: Hamstring (slider → Nordic)

terminal.why: slower eccentric and a lower break point, not more reps

sources: Petersen J et al. (2011), Am J Sports Med
Presland JD et al. (2018), J Sci Med Sport
families.notes: Nordic: 2-3x4-8 then maintenance once a week. DOMS: limit the volume in the first 2 weeks.

technique_ladders.label: Feet (precision and pressure)

levels.description: Flash-1 with one placement and zero noise (board ~7A, vertical ~7A+ for a 7C boulderer; scale to the athlete).
The same rule at flash, plus glued feet on a 40° board.
The rule inside limit work in the weak style (redpoint-1 / redpoint-2): foot held at the first placement on the crux.
Under fatigue and on rock: lead precision at onsight, foot slips per go on a project.

technique_ladders.advance: 2 sessions in a row with ≤ 1 foot readjustment on the sample problem, and benchmark B1 stable or better.
technique_ladders.regress: ≥ 3 readjustments on the sample problem for 2 sessions.
technique_ladders.entry: P1 by default; P2 when the athlete already places the feet once at flash-1.
technique_ladders.measure: Foot readjustments on ONE sample problem per session (video or partner).

technique_ladders.label: Body positioning

levels.description: Board 40-45° around flash+1 with the 3-way position menu.
The menu on the positioning crux of limit problems.
Lead: straight-arm clips and rests found under pump.
On sight: position decided on rock at first sight.

technique_ladders.advance: 2 s hover on the crux in ≥ 4 attempts out of 5 for 2 sessions, or the lead rule kept on 2 routes out of 2.
technique_ladders.measure: Hover 2 s on the crux x/5.

technique_ladders.label: Falls (fear of falling)

levels.description: 1-2 m above the clip. Enables no-take leading.
A fall while moving on a crux. Enables the deliberate fall at the commit point.

technique_ladders.measure: Step, number of falls, max fear 0-10 once per session.
sources: Ilgner A. — The Rock Warrior's Way

untracked_progressions.progression: Anchor +1 sub-grade every 2-3 weeks, or a constraint from the limiter.
Beta forecast: reading 2 → 1 min, then rests and clips predicted.

try_hard.measure: Outcome per key attempt: SEND / FALL / TAKE / LET_GO, plus moves past the point where you wanted to stop (0 / 1 / 2+). Effort 0-3 is optional and secondary.
try_hard.trend: Read on 4 weeks: % of non-sends ending in FALL versus TAKE + LET_GO. Flat for 3 weeks → grade -1 on the comp and no-take, fall ladder one step down (the problem is fear, not difficulty).

limit_weak_style.label: Limit in the weak style
steps: 4 problems or sections of 3-5 moves: 2 power problems as usual, plus 2 chosen because the crux is FEET (small foot to load, lateral press, vertical 5-15°) or POSITION (flag, drop-knee, twist-lock on 40-45°), at redpoint-1 / redpoint-2.
On the 2 technique problems declare one constraint before starting: 'foot placed once' or 'position X on the crux'.
Fixed budget of 5 attempts per problem (a LET_GO uses one), 3 min between attempts, 5 min between problems.
Pre-attempt routine on every attempt; one more move only where the fall is clean onto the mat; breathe out hard on the hard moves.
limit_weak_style.progression: Same problems for 2-3 weeks, then new ones; tighter constraint (smaller feet, less obvious position) before a harder grade.
limit_weak_style.measure: Send yes/no, high point, outcome of non-sends (FALL / TAKE / LET_GO); on the 2 technique problems, foot held at the first placement on the crux yes/no.
limit_weak_style.safety: Never a mono in the gym. One more move never on the high holds of Kilter/Moon, on top-outs, upside down or twisted on one hand.

template_warmup.label: Technique warm-up (zero added minutes)
steps: 3-4 routes or boulders building up to flash-1, each with ONE focus: (1) silent feet, eyes on the foot until it is weighted; (2) hip to the wall and straight arm; (3) a flag or drop-knee where it fits; (4) everything together at normal speed.
template_warmup.measure: None. It is a warm-up, not the technique stimulus.

outdoor_technique_day.label: Outdoor technique day
steps: 1-2 new routes on sight with a beta forecast (timed_route_preview: 2 min reading, sequence said out loud, then predicted yes/no on the key sections).
The project with a commit map.
On vertical sandstone: volume of vertical routes on small feet, the shoe as a variable to test (stiff edging vs soft smearing, one per go), foot slips noted per go.
outdoor_technique_day.measure: Foot slips per go on the project; on sight yes/no.
outdoor_technique_day.safety: Sandstone only ≥ 24 h after rain. First fall of a trip on clean steep terrain, never on a slab.
outdoor_technique_day.finger_hard: only when an attempt is at or above redpoint-2 (stimulus.py OUTDOOR-HARD rule)

pocket_warmup.label: Pocket / mono specific warm-up
steps: pocket_rampup_hangboard: 4 progressive 10 s hangs on the 2- and 3-finger pockets, feet supported, ~50 → 80% bodyweight.
Only for climbers who use monos on rock: single_finger_pocket_rampup, feet always supported, effort ≤ 6/10.
pocket_warmup.when: Before limit work or a rock day with pockets.
pocket_warmup.safety: Submaximal only, on a hangboard pocket only, never a mono in the gym. Watch pulleys and lumbricals of the pocket fingers: any discomfort ends pocket work for the day and is logged as pain 0-3.
sources: Schöffl V et al. (2003), Wilderness Environ Med
